newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil pulp output seen rising up to 3 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Brazil pulp output seen rising up to 3 pct in 1997.

text.p: Brazil's pulp and paper production is expected to grow a maximum of 3 percent in 1997 while world prices are seen rising between 10 and 15 percent, said the Association of Pulp and Paper Manufacturers (ANFPC).

"The stocks in the international markets are falling to normal levels and this is likely to boost prices," said Osmar Zogbi, ANFPC's president, noting that sales next year would rise by 10 percent to roughly $8 billion from $7.4 billion in 1996.

According to Zogbi, Brazil produced 5.7 million metric tonnes of paper and 6.1 million tonnes of pulp in 1996. He expects the volume of Brazilian exports to remain flat next year at 1.2 million tonnes of paper and 2.2 million tonnes of pulp. Currently, Brazil exports 20 percent and 37 percent of its paper and pulp production, respectively, Zogbi said.
Revenue stemming from exports, however, is expected to increase to a maximum of 15 percent, following the expected rise in international pulp and paper prices, he noted.
He said Brazilian pulp and paper companies invested $3 billion in 1996 to expand production and increase competition, noting that the sector plans to invest and additional $10.8 billion by 2005.
Brazil, the world's seventh largest pulp and paper producer, has 220 pulp and paper manufacturers whose production accounts for 1.3 percent of the country's GDP, he said.
